solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A saint is repeatedly going around his town?

indicators.note: going around tells us the doubled word is turned to run backwards
repeatedly asks for the little word is to be written twice over

explanation.surface: A holy man keeps travelling round and round the place he comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles the word and 'going around' turns the pair backwards; 'his town' points to the saint's own home, St Francis's.
explanation.definitionFit: Assisi in Umbria is the hometown of St Francis, the saint whose town the clue points to.

clue.text: A second amount of money? Ecstasy! Take it!

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for second, a unit of time
a sum is an amount of money
E is slang shorthand for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone is offered a further cash payment and an illicit pill and told to grab it.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something as given is to suppose it is true without proof.

clue.text: Very tiny coat — bum is suffering!

indicators.note: suffering suggests the letters before it are battered out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that a skimpy jacket leaves someone's backside out in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' belongs to the fodder: COAT BUM IS has the nine letters needed, so only 'suffering' signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something smaller than an atom is extremely small, so the adjective serves for minute.

clue.text: Members with ability to survive rough voyages

definitions.text: Members with ability to survive rough voyages

parts.words: Members with ability to survive rough voyages
parts.note: members are limbs, and these are the ones that keep a sailor upright on a rolling deck

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the ability to keep one's balance and avoid seasickness aboard ship, pictured as limbs.

clue.text: Irregular picadors getting into trouble

indicators.note: getting into trouble suggests the word picadors is thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Bullfight horsemen now and then come to grief in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens only at scattered, uneven intervals is occasional and irregular.

clue.text: Food on plane journey is something you'd dream of being good

definitions.text: something you'd dream of being good

parts.note: a pie is a kind of food
while flying on a plane you are up in the sky

explanation.surface: In-flight catering is described as the stuff of dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: The meal eaten at altitude is literally a pie up in the sky; the idiom means a hoped-for good thing that will never arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an appealing prospect that is unrealistic, something wished for rather than likely.

clue.text: Rescue organisation is blocking street making people prejudiced

parts.note: the RAC (Royal Automobile Club) is a British breakdown rescue service for motorists

indicators.note: blocking here means the word is closes off the street on both sides, surrounding it

explanation.surface: A roadside recovery team shuts a road and turns out to be full of bigots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' has the little word closing off the street from both ends; the RAC is a British motoring rescue body.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who are prejudiced against people of other races are bigots of that particular kind.

clue.text: Make a hole in material

definitions.meaning: to bore through something with a rotating tool
a hard-wearing twilled cotton fabric of that name

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for boring with a bit and the name of a heavy cotton twill cloth.

clue.text: Cleric, fool in church producing split

indicators.note: in says the cleric and fool are placed inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A priest and an idiot cause a schism in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep crack or fissure in a glacier is a split in the ice.

clue.text: Twist vehicle around in underground tunnel

indicators.note: around turns the whole run of the two words to read backwards

parts.note: to yaw is to twist or swing off a straight course
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car spins round while inside a tunnel below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns both pieces together, the twist first; 'Twist' looks like the anagram signal but is the nautical verb, to swing off course.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain this is a pedestrian passage under a road; in America it is an underground railway.

clue.text: Give account of some French bed to English

parts.note: des is French for some
a crib is a child's bed
E is the abbreviation for English, added at the end

explanation.surface: Someone explains about a French bed being brought over to England.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an account of something is to portray it in words.

clue.text: Damaged net at home could be this

definitions.text: Damaged net at home could be this

indicators.note: damaged suggests the words net at home are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A fishing net left in the house may well end up full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi-all-in-one: the whole clue defines, with 'Damaged' also the anagram signal for NET AT HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric eaten into by clothes-moth larvae is holey and worn, as a stored net might be.

clue.text: Destroying Spooner's courageous community

indicators.note: Spooner's means the first sounds of two words are swapped, after the Rev Spooner

parts.note: daring means courageous
a town is a community

explanation.surface: A brave neighbourhood is being demolished.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the D and T of DARING TOWN gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Demolishing a building is pulling it to the ground, destroying it.

clue.text: Dance as part of rehearsal, say

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something danced as a section of a practice run, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American partner dance with origins in Cuban music.

clue.text: State must act as she's in a mess

indicators.note: in a mess suggests the letters of the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman is in a muddle and must do something about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A New England state of the USA, whose capital is Boston.

clue.text: Don't agree to buy edition of magazine?

definitions.meaning: to dispute or challenge what someone says
read literally, to take a copy of a periodical's number

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to disagree, and literally it describes acquiring an edition of a periodical.

clue.text: Special constable on avenue, one character going wrong in search

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for special constable, a volunteer British police officer

indicators.note: one character going wrong says a single letter of the avenue is replaced by another

parts.note: the word avenue taken as written

explanation.surface: A volunteer policeman on a street hunts for something while one person misbehaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one character going wrong' changes the U of AVENUE to G.
explanation.definitionFit: To scavenge is to rummage or search for usable things among waste.

clue.text: Bird ends with sign of approval, being something offered with nibbles

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
tails are ends
a tick is a mark of approval

explanation.surface: A bird finishes up with a nod of approval at a party snack table.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pointed stick used to spear and offer canapés and other party nibbles.

clue.text: Experimental set-up to examine what sleeping conditions might be like?

definitions.meaning: equipment or a place used for trialling new machinery or systems

definitions.text: to examine what sleeping conditions might be like?
definitions.meaning: read literally, a trial of a bed to see how well one sleeps

explanation.definitionFit: A rig for trialling new equipment, and literally a bed being tried out for comfort.

clue.text: Rough during performance, grabbing old lover

indicators.note: grabbing means the first part seizes and holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: during a performance an actor is in act, on stage in a section of the play
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A rough moment on stage as a former partner is seized mid-show.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough estimate is approximate and not precise.

clue.text: Lands in which you'll find authentic Modern Miss

parts.note: real means authentic
Ms is the modern title for a woman, used in place of Miss

explanation.surface: Kingdoms where a genuine contemporary young woman is to be found.
explanation.definitionFit: Realms are kingdoms or domains, lands ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Beautiful female from America following archdeacon

indicators.note: following places America's letters after the archdeacon's

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
US stands for the United States

explanation.surface: A lovely American woman walks behind a senior churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman goddess of love is the byword for a beautiful woman.

clue.text: Explosive that's inert surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly hints that the letters of inert end up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: An explosive that turns out, against expectation, to be harmless.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate, saltpetre, is a key ingredient of gunpowder.

clue.text: Sweet liquid taken round by Reg nicely

indicators.note: taken round suggests the letters of Reg nicely are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Reg kindly carries a sugary drink round.
explanation.definitionFit: A colourless, syrupy, sweet-tasting liquid used in food and cosmetics.

clue.text: Computer turned on needs to be working all right

indicators.note: turned means the little word on is read backwards
working suggests the words to be are worked into a new order

parts.note: OK means all right

explanation.surface: A machine that is switched on has to be running properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives NO; 'working' rearranges TO BE into TEBO.
explanation.definitionFit: A small portable laptop computer is sold under this name.

clue.text: Female gets various medals

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of medals take a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman collects a number of awards.
explanation.definitionFit: A damsel is an archaic word for a young woman.

clue.text: In the final bit this writer is improving

indicators.note: In at the start says the writer goes inside the final bit

parts.note: an ending is the final bit
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The author says he is polishing the last part of his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Emending a text is correcting and so improving it.

clue.text: Focus attention on son with long hair

parts.note: a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone concentrates on their son's flowing locks.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise a point is to put weight or emphasis on it.
